solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Miscue Mr Bach corrected — in some of his pieces? (12, two words)

indicators.note: a miscue that is corrected gets put right, so the letters are set in a new and proper order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician fluffs a passage and gets Bach put right, during one of his works.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of MISCUE MR BACH spell CHAMBER MUSIC, and Bach wrote plenty of it, so the question mark covers the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach composed many works for small ensembles, the genre known as chamber music, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Jokily woman soprano follows choir copies

blocks.note: CH is a dictionary abbreviation for choir
to ape is to copy or mimic
S is the standard abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A woman soprano comes in after the choir, imitating them.
explanation.walkthrough: The soprano's S follows the other pieces, so it comes last. CHAPESS is a facetious feminine of chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the term as a humorous feminine form of chap, hence a woman said jokily.

clue.text: Coloured rock, confection of Hershey (10 p)

indicators.note: a confection is something mixed up and made, so the letters that follow are concocted afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
the number written out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seaside rock, a coloured sweet, seemingly made by Hershey and priced at ten pence.
explanation.walkthrough: Hershey is an American chocolate maker, which suits the sweet-shop picture; rock here is geology, not candy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypersthene is a green or brownish pyroxene mineral found in igneous rocks, so a coloured rock-forming material.

clue.text: A shade of crimson fashion one comes up with

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: Someone devises a red shade along with a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Modena is a deep purplish-crimson colour, named after the Italian city.

clue.text: Chicken flesh I had instead of duck

indicators.note: this phrase says one piece is to take the place of another inside the word

blocks.note: flesh as in the body
contraction of I had
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A diner chose chicken meat rather than duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the O of BODY for ID to get BIDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Biddy is a dialect or affectionate word for a hen or chick.

clue.text: US fish from river one with no fixed 'ome there swallows almost whole

indicators.note: dropping the aitch from home shows that the person is to lose the letter H
to swallow something is to take it inside
almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
a hobo has no fixed home, here losing its first letter
all means the whole

explanation.surface: A wandering angler's catch: an American fish found in a river by a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped aitch of 'ome is the hint to drop that letter from the homeless one; almost trims the last letter off whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Robalo is the name used in America for the snook, a game fish of warm coastal waters.

clue.text: Like some meat old fool found under inverted pot?

indicators.note: something inverted is turned upside down, which in a down entry means read upwards

blocks.note: a pot belly is a tum
tony is an obsolete word for a simpleton

explanation.surface: A daft old character is discovered beneath an upturned cooking pot, like a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the fool sits under the pot, so the pot's piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Muttony means tasting or smelling of mutton, a description of some meat.

clue.text: Don sari that's creased? It might have benefited from this

definitions.text: It might have benefited from this

indicators.note: a creased garment has been crumpled out of shape, so these letters are crumpled into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Put on a crumpled sari? It could have done with pressing first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a verb, to put on clothes, but it is just fodder. The definition refers back to the creased sari.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadiron is a heavy flat iron for smoothing cloth, just what a creased sari needs.

clue.text: Candle fulfilling a bit of work in Church

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other here

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
the erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A candle doing its small job in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerge is an old spelling of serge, a large wax candle used in church.

clue.text: Most of St Laurent's weight lies behind what's excellent for audience re special gear

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is chosen by its sound
most of a word is all but its last letter

blocks.note: high, as in high quality, means excellent
poids is French for weight, fitting a Frenchman such as Yves St Laurent

explanation.surface: A designer's weight problem, set beside excellence, has something to do with gearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lies behind puts the French piece after the sound-alike piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypoid gear is a spiral bevel gear with offset axes, used in car rear axles.

clue.text: E.g. tributes, central portion thereof given over for divinity

indicators.note: only the middle part of the word is the one to act on, its outer letters staying put
something turned over is flipped, so this part is read in the other direction

blocks.note: tributes are an example of dues, payments owed

explanation.surface: Offerings to a god, with their middle portion handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle of DUES, UE, is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Deus is Latin for god, a deity or divinity.

clue.text: Sandy's legacy, not in mature years

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in
age is one's mature years

explanation.surface: An inheritance from someone called Sandy, received while still young.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy is not a person but Hurricane Sandy of 2012, which left millions without electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A power cut left behind by the hurricane Sandy is an outage, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Rough motoring with ice concerning direction-finders?

indicators.note: a rough version is disordered, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Driving badly on an icy road, perhaps worried about sat-navs.
explanation.definitionFit: A goniometer measures angles, and radio goniometers serve as direction-finders, so the adjective relates to them.

clue.text: Jock's owed what's accrued, including crazy bet

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the word next to it is jumbled
including means holding something within

blocks.note: what has accrued has been added
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's debts pile up, including a reckless wager.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock's signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Addebted is an old Scots form of indebted, meaning owing money.

clue.text: Metalworker hammers with this stylus on end of handle

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a stylus is a writing instrument, a pen
last letter of handle

explanation.surface: A metalworker uses a tool with a pointed tip on the end of its handle.
explanation.walkthrough: Pene is a variant spelling of peen.
explanation.definitionFit: The peen is the thin or rounded striking end of a hammerhead opposite the face, used to shape metal.

clue.text: Having a nap when do's lacking vitality

indicators.note: lacking means without, so these letters are taken away

blocks.note: dozing is having a nap
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sleeping through a party that has no life in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do's' reads as do is; a do looks like a party but the word is just removed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Zing is liveliness or zest, a synonym for vitality.

clue.text: One of the 'kindly ones' is not, as of old, supporting return of anger

indicators.note: return means going back, so this word is read backwards

blocks.note: ire is anger
nys is an archaic, Spenserian contraction of is not

explanation.surface: One of the gentle ones is anything but, propping up returning fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The Furies were euphemistically called the Eumenides, the kindly ones; supporting puts the archaic word after the reversed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Erinys is the singular name for one of the Furies, the avenging goddesses called the kindly ones by euphemism.

clue.text: African bird that's showy in colour, I expect

indicators.note: showy is read as shows, so the following words show the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: An African bird with bright plumage, I imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showy' looks like a description of the bird's plumage but signals that the answer is on show in what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A lourie, or turaco, is a brightly coloured fruit-eating bird of African forests.

clue.text: What's done with traffic getting round outdated signs?

indicators.note: to get round something is to surround it

blocks.note: traffic is made up of cars
an act is a thing done

explanation.surface: A question about the purpose of old road signs placed around traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracts is an obsolete form of characts, meaning characters or written marks.

clue.text: Part of après-ski wear maybe, low and not restricting personal pong! (8, two words)

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
taken as written
BO is body odour, a personal smell

explanation.surface: Après-ski clothes that are feeling down and do nothing to contain a smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Pong is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon boot is a thick padded boot worn in snow, typical après-ski footwear.

clue.text: Minimum of make-up applied to face — it's fashionable

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, a single opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of make-up
on as in put on, applied to
dial is slang for a face

explanation.surface: A little make-up on the face is the latest thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mondial, from French mondial, worldwide, is listed in Chambers in the sense of fashionable or worldly.

clue.text: Meddling? Infer in parts cut that will get to this old comic playwright

indicators.note: cut means removed, and in parts says the removal happens in separate chunks

blocks.note: meddling is interference
taken as written, removed in two parts

explanation.surface: Deduce, from meddling with scenes cut, which Roman playwright this is.
explanation.walkthrough: In parts means IN and FER come out separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman writer of comedies in the second century BC, an old comic playwright.

clue.text: Domain of Polish nobleman, corrupt Tsar's toy

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoilt and altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Polish lord's estate, the plaything of a corrupt Russian emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: A starosty was the district or estate held by a starost, a Polish noble governor.

clue.text: Make an image of princess, emblematic in part

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words just before, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across these two words

clue.text: Acacia giving a bit of shade over garden path

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a small piece, its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of shade
an allée is a tree-lined garden walk

clue.text: Mouse's tail is out of place in this church alcove?

explanation.definitionFit: A shrine can be a recess or niche in a church holding a relic or image.

clue.text: Sort of pen, see

clue.text: Former king, idle at heart? One puts a gloss on things

blocks.note: GR, Georgius Rex, King George

clue.text: Good story (if sometimes untrue), omitting end — clever

clue.text: Noun in this may be rendered Anglice?

clue.text: Died single — former knowledge I lost — it's often planned (cynically?)
